LLM_description:
Situation:
The division is conducting sustained offensive operations across a contested river corridor. Maneuver elements are pushing on multiple axes while artillery and fires units support deep strikes. Ground lines of communication are subject to interdiction and observation, with the valley floor vulnerable to indirect fire and the mountain pass to the east prone to rockfall and ambush. Air resupply is limited due to adverse weather and enemy air defense coverage. Several rear-area depots, including Supply Depot Bravo and Logistics Hub Echo, must push ammunition, fuel, and medical materiel forward to units such as Infantry Battalion Charlie, Armored Squadron Fox, and Artillery Battery Sierra at dispersed forward operating bases. Daily consumptions fluctuate with engagement intensity, and some stocks are rationed. Road networks include choke points at bridges and cutbanks; convoy movement windows are restricted to reduce exposure.

Mission:
Resupply all designated forward units with critical classes of supply while minimizing total operational cost, which includes transport costs, shortage penalty costs, vehicle deployment costs, and fixed route security risk costs.

Execution/Concept:
- Prioritize essential commodities to maintain combat power and medical support. Plan daily flows from depots to forward units by commodity and route, synchronized with maneuver and fires timelines.
- Depot release is constrained by on-hand stocks per supply type by day; outbound flows from any depot cannot exceed available inventory.
- Unit demand must be covered by delivered flow or recorded as shortfall. Any shortfall is explicitly penalized to discourage unmet essential needs while allowing risk-informed trade-offs when routes are compromised.
- Load planning is volumetric. Each commodity has a distinct packing factor; total loaded volume per depot–unit route cannot exceed the sum of assigned vehicle capacities. Vehicle dispatches are integer-valued and represent whole vehicles committed to a route on a given day.
- Vehicles can only move on activated routes. Activating any depot–unit route on any day incurs a fixed Risk Cost, reflecting security overhead (engineer route clearance, EOD, escort teams, ISR overwatch, and communications control). This Risk Cost is charged once per route/day regardless of how many vehicles are sent on that route.
- The fleet is finite. Total vehicles dispatched across all routes on a given day cannot exceed fleet availability. Vehicle deployment cost captures fuel, maintenance, crew time, and readiness impacts.
- Transport costs vary by route, commodity, and distance. Risk exposure on certain corridors drives higher fixed route activation costs. The plan seeks to consolidate flows onto fewer activated routes to amortize fixed risk overhead where feasible, while opening additional routes when required to meet demands or bypass hazards.
- Terrain and threat considerations: bridge load limits constrain heavy traffic; single-lane segments require time separation; the valley corridor is intermittently under indirect fire; the mountain pass may be closed due to rockfall; route clearance assets are limited and must be scheduled. Coordination with Military Police and Engineers is required to sequence escorts and clearance. Movement is deconflicted with maneuver to avoid congestion and fratricide.
